page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmsv2 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs, 1 physical core with hyper-threading (2 threads per core), and a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with a massive 168.0 GB of memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2348.0 and strong single-threaded compression results, such as 34.74 GB/sec in gzip. However, due to the low core count, multi-core performance is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 2217.38 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2886.0, both falling into lower percentiles. Memory performance also shows a tradeoff: while the capacity is vast, large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths are relatively low at 21.36 GB/sec and 14.38 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8-2ms_v2 offers a highly specialized resource profile, providing massive memory capacity without forcing the acquisition of unnecessary CPU cores. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for memory-bound applications that do not scale with high parallel compute. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded data processing, memory-intensive caching, lightweight database operations, and applications requiring large in-memory datasets but minimal concurrent CPU utilization.
